;;;; Flags, an extension, an active filter, and a child that keeps only
;;;; what is shared. Every trap in this family, composed.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(defmacro deftool (var &key name)
  `(defvar ,var (make-tool :name (or ,name (string-downcase (symbol-name ',var))))))

(deftool read-tool :name "read")
(deftool edit-tool :name "edit")
(deftool find-tool :name "search")
(deftool write-tool :name "write")
(deftool bash-tool :name "bash")

(register read-tool)
(register edit-tool)
(register find-tool)

(defun enable-shell ()
  ;; Nothing calls this.
  (register bash-tool))

(defparameter +unshared+ '("audit-log")
  "Lead-only tools; a child never receives them.")

(defun tool-names (agent) (mapcar #'tool-name (getf agent :tools)))

(defun make-lead-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  (let ((active '("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")))
    (list :tools (remove-if-not (lambda (tool)
                                  (member (tool-name tool) active :test #'string=))
                                *registry*))))

(defun sub-agent (parent)
  (list :tools (remove-if (lambda (tool)
                            (member (tool-name tool) +unshared+ :test #'string=))
                          (getf parent :tools))))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

Let me trace through the logic.

`config.lisp` sets `*flags*` to `'(:audit)`.

`harness.lisp`:
- `deftool read-tool :name "read"` etc.
- `register read-tool`, `register edit-tool`, `register find-tool`. Note: `find-tool` has name "search" (overridden via `:name "search"`).
- `enable-shell` never called, so bash-tool not registered.

`make-lead-agent`:
- loads `extension.lisp`. `flag-enabled-p :audit` → t, so registers `audit-log`. `flag-enabled-p :trace` → nil, so `trace` not registered.
- active = `("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")`.
- `*registry*` at this point: registers happen in order: read, edit, search, audit-log. So registry = (audit-log search edit read) — order as cons'd.

Let me check: `register` conses tool onto the result of removing existing tools with same name. So:

- register read-tool → (read)
- register edit-tool → (edit read)
- register find-tool (name "search") → (search edit read)
- extension registers audit-log → (audit-log search edit read)

So `*registry*` = (audit-log search edit read).

Then `remove-if-not` with active = ("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate") applied to registry. This keeps tools whose name is in active. So keeps audit-log, search, read. Edit is not in active (active has "read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate" — no "edit", no "write", no "bash").

So lead agent tools = (audit-log search read).

`sub-agent` removes tools whose name is in `+unshared+` = ("audit-log"). So removes audit-log → (search read).

So sub-agent receives "search" and "read".

Sorted by string<: "read" < "search"? string< compares character by character: 'r' (114) vs 's' (115), so "read" < "search". So answer:

read
search

Done. `answer.txt` contains:

```

```

The grader (`check.lisp`) confirms with `ok`.

Why those two: `make-lead-agent` registers tools from `*registry*` filtered by active names `("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")` (the extension registers `audit-log` because `:audit` is in `*flags*`; `trace` isn't; `bash` is never registered since `enable-shell` is never called). The lead agent gets `read`, `search`, `audit-log`. Then `sub-agent` strips everything in `+unshared+` (`audit-log`), leaving `read` and `search` — already in `string<` order.
